patients.summary: Healthy elementary school teacher who joined in 2021. Endometriosis diagnosed clinically by gynecology in 2023 with a left endometrioma; laparoscopy declined; after a break the couple resumed trying in late 2024, and a 2026 infertility workup is normal, with a reproductive endocrinology referral open today.

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called after school hours asking to establish with the practice. Teaches second grade locally, had been driving back to her old primary care office for appointments and would like someone closer. Membership agreement and welcome packet emailed. Records release for prior primary care office completed by e-signature, faxed today. New patient physical booked 10/5 at 7:30 am, before her school day. Asked her to come fasting.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27 y/o woman establishing care. Previously followed at a primary care office about an hour away; records requested.

No ongoing medical problems. Never hospitalized. No surgeries. No meds other than ibuprofen for period cramps, a day or two each cycle. NKDA.

GYN: menarche in her early teens, cycles regular about monthly, cramping usually the first day or two, manageable with OTC ibuprofen. No bleeding between periods. Married, one partner. Never had a pelvic infection or STI. Last Pap 2020 per patient, normal. Not currently trying to conceive; may in the next year or two.

Family: mother has endometriosis. Mother's sister had trouble getting pregnant. No known heart disease, diabetes or cancer in parents.

Social: teaches elementary school. Married. Never a smoker. Does not drink. Walks most evenings.

ROS: negative except as above. Mood good. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: well-appearing. Vitals per flowsheet, BMI about 22. HEENT clear. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Skin without concerning lesions. No edema. Pelvic not done today, Pap not due.

A/P: healthy adult, preventive care.
- Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening, she agrees.
- Flu vaccine given today. COVID primary series done in the spring per patient, card on file to be scanned with outside records.
- Tdap was within 10 years per her recollection; will confirm from records.
- Pap due 2023.
- Period cramps on ibuprofen as needed, fine for now; let me know if it changes.
- Return in a year, or sooner by text or call.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Melissa, everything from Tuesday came back fine: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, sugar and cholesterol are all in the normal range. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do. Good to have you with us.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Received by fax, 23 pages, from her previous primary care office. Abstracted:
- Problem list: none active.
- Medications: none.
- Allergies: NKDA.
- Cervical cytology 07/2020: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
- Immunizations: Tdap 08/2017. COVID-19 Pfizer 03/27/2021 and 04/17/2021 (from scanned vaccination card).
- Last physical 07/2020, unremarkable.
Immunizations entered. Scanned to media. Routed to PCP for review.

documents.title: Question about summer camp form
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I'm helping run the district's summer reading camp this year and they want a health form signed by a doctor. Do I need to come in or can I drop it off? Thanks, Melissa

documents.title: Re: Question about summer camp form
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Melissa, you were just seen in October, so you can upload it here or drop it at the front desk. Doctor will sign and we'll message you when it's ready, usually within two business days.

documents.title: Annual visit reminder
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Melissa, it's time to schedule your yearly physical. Flu and COVID boosters for this season are in stock and can be given at the same visit. Reply with a few early mornings that suit you.

documents.title: Re: Annual visit reminder
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Any morning the week of Oct 10 before 8 works. Thank you!

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Doing well. School year off to a busy start.

Interval: no illnesses, no ED or urgent care. Still uses ibuprofen for cramps at the start of each period; says they have been a bit worse over the past year or so but still manageable, does not miss work. Cycles regular. No bleeding between periods.

She and her husband are planning to start trying for a pregnancy this fall. Asked what she should do beforehand. Talked through: keep up with vaccines (flu and COVID today, both fine before and during pregnancy), and she already avoids alcohol and tobacco. Advised to call when she has a positive test so we can get her connected with obstetrics. Mother's history of endometriosis and aunt's infertility noted again; nothing to do about it now unless trying takes longer than expected, in which case she should tell us.

Meds: none. NKDA.
PHQ-2 0.

Exam: vitals as charted, BMI 22. Well-appearing. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema.

A/P: healthy, planning pregnancy. Vaccines given. Pap due next year. Labs from last fall were normal; none today. Annual next fall.

documents.title: Period pain
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I wanted to see if I could come in about my periods. The cramps have gotten a lot worse, the first couple of days I'm curled up with a heating pad and the ibuprofen barely touches it. Sex has also started to hurt, deep inside, which is new. We've been trying to get pregnant since the fall with no luck. Not sure if any of that is connected but it's on my mind. After school any day works. Melissa

documents.title: Re: Period pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for writing, Melissa. Those things may well be connected and it's worth sorting out. Let's do Tuesday 5/2 at 3:45. If the pain gets much worse or you get fever, text me before then.

orders.reason: progressive dysmenorrhea and dyspareunia, trying to conceive 7 months, family history of endometriosis

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for worsening period pain.

Over roughly two years her periods have hurt more each year. Now the first two or three days are bad: dull cramping low in the pelvis that goes into the low back and sometimes toward the rectum. Ibuprofen takes the edge off but not much more. Over the last several months, deep pain with intercourse. Some discomfort with bowel movements around her period; otherwise bowels normal, no blood. Cycles still regular, every 28 to 30 days. No spotting between periods, no unusual discharge. No fever. No urinary symptoms.

Trying to conceive since about September, 7 months now.

No prior pelvic infections or STIs. No surgeries. Mother with endometriosis.

Exam: comfortable. Vitals as charted. Abdomen soft, mild suprapubic tenderness without guarding, no masses. Urine hCG negative today. I did not do a pelvic exam today; she would rather have that done once by gynecology.

A/P: progressive secondary-sounding dysmenorrhea with deep dyspareunia and cyclic bowel discomfort, plus a family history: endometriosis is the leading concern. Seven months of trying is still within the normal window, but given the picture it is reasonable for gynecology to look at both together.
- Referral to gynecology; front desk to help schedule.
- Ibuprofen with food at the first sign of her period, heat.
- Call if pain becomes constant, fever, or she misses a period.

documents.title: Gynecology referral scheduled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Referral and 5/2 office note faxed to the outside gynecology group. Their scheduler called back: new patient consult Friday 6/9 at 9:30, ultrasound same visit if needed. Patient notified by text and confirmed.

events.reason: chronic pelvic pain and difficulty conceiving

conditions.label: Endometriosis
conditions.note: clinical diagnosis by gynecology; left ovarian cyst on ultrasound; laparoscopy recommended

reports.text:
TRANSVAGINAL PELVIC ULTRASOUND
Indication: pelvic pain, dysmenorrhea, difficulty conceiving.
Technique: transvaginal grayscale and color Doppler imaging.
Uterus: retroverted, normal in size and contour. Endometrium normal in thickness for cycle phase. No myometrial mass.
Right ovary: normal in size with normal follicles.
Left ovary: a homogeneous hypoechoic cyst measuring 4.0 x 3.6 x 3.4 cm, without internal vascularity or solid component.
No free fluid in the pelvis.
reports.conclusion: Normal uterus. 4 cm homogeneous hypoechoic left ovarian cyst.

documents.title: Gynecology Consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY GROUP
Consultation, date of visit 06/09/2023
Referred by her primary care physician.

Reason: pelvic pain and trouble conceiving.

Ms. Nolan is a 29-year-old who describes two years of steadily worsening menstrual pain, at its worst during the first two to three days of flow. The pain is a dull cramp that can spread into the lower back and toward the rectum. Deep penetration during intercourse has become painful, enough that intimacy has become a source of stress. Around menses she also notices pain with defecation; bowel pattern is otherwise unchanged. Over-the-counter analgesics have helped only modestly. Menses are regular at 28 to 30 day intervals with no intermenstrual bleeding or abnormal discharge. She and her husband have been attempting pregnancy for eight months.

PMH: no pelvic inflammatory disease or sexually transmitted infection.
PSH: none; no abdominal operations.
Medications: none.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: endometriosis in her mother; infertility in a maternal aunt.
Social: nonsmoker, no alcohol. Otherwise healthy.

Exam: well-appearing. External genitalia normal. Speculum: normal cervix, physiologic discharge. Bimanual and rectovaginal: uterus retroverted; tenderness on palpation of the posterior cul-de-sac with nodularity along the uterosacral ligaments.

Transvaginal ultrasound in clinic today: normal uterus; a homogeneous hypoechoic 4 cm cyst on the left ovary.

Impression: findings are highly suggestive of endometriosis, with a probable left ovarian endometrioma, in a patient with dysmenorrhea, deep dyspareunia, cyclic dyschezia and eight months of attempting conception.

Plan: I recommended diagnostic laparoscopy, which would confirm and stage the disease and allow treatment of implants and the cyst at the same sitting. We discussed what surgery involves and its recovery. She would like time to think it over with her husband and will call our surgical scheduler if she wishes to proceed. Continue analgesics as needed in the meantime.

Thank you for the referral.

Allergies: NKDA

documents.title: Outside gynecology consult received
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Gyn consult reviewed. Exam and ultrasound support endometriosis with a left endometrioma, 4 cm. Laparoscopy recommended; patient deciding. Endometriosis added to problem list. Will check in with her.

documents.title: Follow-up after gynecology consult
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called to see how the gyn visit went and to answer questions. She understood the diagnosis and the recommendation for laparoscopy. After talking it over at home they have decided not to schedule surgery right now; she does not want an operation this summer, and they are going to take a break from trying for a while. She knows the surgery offer stands and can go back to gynecology whenever she is ready. Pain plan for now: ibuprofen with food early in the period, heat. Agreed she will reach out if pain worsens or when they are ready to try again. Problem list updated.

reports.text:
Specimen: cervical, liquid-based preparation.
Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; endocervical/transformation zone component present.
Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, Pap due.

Endometriosis: diagnosed clinically by gyn in June, left endometrioma 4 cm on ultrasound. She did not go ahead with laparoscopy. They are not trying to conceive at the moment. Periods still painful the first couple of days; ibuprofen with food and heat get her through, has not missed school for it. Intercourse still uncomfortable at times. Bowels normal.

Meds: OTC ibuprofen with periods only. NKDA.
PHQ-9: 2. Says she is fine, the summer decision was hard but she feels settled about it.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, BMI 22. Heart, lungs normal. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: normal external exam, cervix normal, Pap collected. Deferred bimanual.

A/P:
- Endometriosis: stable on current approach. She knows the door to gyn is open.
- Cervical cancer screening: Pap today.
- Flu and updated COVID given.
- Return for annual next fall.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Melissa, your Pap was normal. With your age and history the next one is due in three years.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit. Canceled the spring check-in, nothing was wrong.

Endometriosis: periods unchanged from last year, painful the first two days, ibuprofen and heat. No missed work. Dyspareunia comes and goes. They plan to start trying again around the end of the year. We talked about what to expect: given the endometriosis, if no pregnancy within about six months to a year she should come back sooner rather than later and we will get her back to gyn. She would rather avoid surgery if she can but is open to hearing options again.

Meds: OTC ibuprofen with menses. NKDA. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: vitals as charted, BMI 23. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft, nontender, no mass.

A/P:
- Endometriosis, stable symptoms. Plan as above.
- CBC and lipids today (screening, last 2021).
- Flu and COVID today.
- Pap 2023 normal, next 2026.

orders.reason: endometriosis with worsening pain; trying to conceive about 10 months

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual visit, and she wants to talk about the endometriosis.

Since about the spring, the pain has stepped up: cramps now start a few days before her period and hang on through the last day of bleeding, and ibuprofen is not enough. Deep pain with intercourse is worse over the same six months. Cycles regular, about every 28 days, bleeding around five days.

They started trying again last December, about ten months without a pregnancy. She is ready to go back to gyn and hear the options, including surgery.

Meds: OTC ibuprofen with menses. NKDA.
PHQ-9: 3. Frustrated but coping; good support at home.

Exam: vitals as charted, BMI 23. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft, mild lower abdominal tenderness, no mass, no guarding. Urine hCG negative.

A/P:
- Endometriosis with worsening pain while trying to conceive: re-referral to the same gynecology group so they can pick up where they left off in 2023.
- CBC and metabolic panel today.
- Flu and COVID today.
- Pap due next year.
- I'll watch for their letter.

documents.title: Gynecology Follow-up
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY GROUP
Office visit 12/15/2025
Re: Melissa Nolan, DOB 12/09/1993

Ms. Nolan returns to our practice, last seen in June 2023, when her pelvic pain and difficulty conceiving were first evaluated and endometriosis was diagnosed on clinical grounds. She did not proceed with laparoscopy at that time.

She now has severe cramping pelvic pain that starts several days before menses and persists until bleeding stops. Deep dyspareunia has steadily worsened over the last six months. Cycles are regular, every 28 days with 5 days of flow. The couple has been trying to conceive for one year. She takes no medications at present.

Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother with endometriosis; maternal aunt with infertility.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, elementary school teacher.

Exam: abdomen soft. Bimanual examination elicits tenderness; the uterus is retroverted and fixed. No adnexal mass is felt.

Labs drawn today: CBC, TSH with free T4, and prolactin, all within normal limits.

Assessment: secondary dysmenorrhea and deep dyspareunia due to endometriosis; one year of attempting conception.

Plan:
1. Naproxen 500 mg twice daily with food, starting a day or two before expected menses and through the heaviest days. Hormonal suppression is not appropriate while she is trying to conceive.
2. Return in about three weeks with pelvic ultrasound and further evaluation.

Thank you for allowing us to share in her care.

reports.text:
PELVIC ULTRASOUND, TRANSABDOMINAL AND TRANSVAGINAL
Indication: endometriosis, abnormal uterine bleeding, pelvic pain.
Uterus: normal in size. Endometrium normal in thickness. No focal myometrial lesion.
Ovaries: multiple cystic masses are present on both ovaries, each with diffuse low-level internal echoes giving a ground-glass appearance, without solid components or internal flow.
No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Multiple ground-glass cystic masses on both ovaries, in keeping with endometriomas. Normal-sized uterus.

documents.title: Gynecology Follow-up
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY GROUP
Office visit 01/06/2026

Follow-up for endometriosis, seen here a month ago for severe menstrual cramps and before that for fertility concerns.

She describes six months of abnormal bleeding, which on questioning is spotting in the days before her period and heavier flow than she used to have; cycles remain regular. Periods continue to grow more painful, with pelvic discomfort between them and painful intercourse. Trying to conceive for about a year. Using naproxen with menses.

Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: uterus normal in size. Nodularity of the uterosacral ligaments.

CA-125: 61 U/mL (reference under 35), elevated.

Ultrasound today: multiple cystic ovarian masses bilaterally with a ground-glass appearance, consistent with endometriomas.

Assessment: endometriosis with bilateral ovarian endometriomas; the CA-125 elevation fits this picture.

Plan: return next month for a dedicated infertility evaluation. Continue naproxen.

Thank you for allowing us to share in her care.

reports.text:
TRANSVAGINAL PELVIC ULTRASOUND
Indication: infertility, endometriosis.
Uterus: normal in size and contour. Endometrium normal for cycle day.
Left ovary: homogeneous hypoechoic cyst measuring 4.1 x 3.5 x 3.3 cm without internal flow or solid component.
Right ovary: no dominant cyst.
No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Normal-sized uterus. Homogeneous hypoechoic left ovarian cyst, 4.1 cm.

documents.title: Infertility Evaluation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY GROUP
Infertility consultation, 02/09/2026

Ms. Nolan comes back to our clinic to continue her infertility evaluation. Her earlier visits here were for chronic pelvic pain, severe dysmenorrhea and abnormal bleeding.

She and her partner have been attempting pregnancy for 14 months. Cycles come every 27 to 30 days and are reliably painful, most of all on the first two days of flow. She has intermittent lower abdominal discomfort that intensifies near her period. On direct questioning she notes occasional pain with deep penetration and some pelvic pain with bowel movements close to menses; she has had no rectal bleeding and no change in the caliber of her stools.

PSH: none; no abdominal surgery.
Allergies: NKDA.
Medications: naproxen with menses.

Exam: mild tenderness with deep palpation of the posterior vaginal fornix.

Transvaginal ultrasound: normal-sized uterus; a homogeneous hypoechoic cyst on the left ovary.

Assessment: infertility of 14 months in a 32-year-old with endometriosis.

Plan:
1. Cervical NAAT for chlamydia and gonorrhea today.
2. Home urinary LH kits for the next several cycles to document ovulation.
3. Hysterosalpingogram in the follicular phase.
4. Endometrial biopsy in the luteal phase.
5. Semen analysis for her partner.
We will review everything together once complete.

Thank you for allowing us to share in her care.

reports.text:
SPECIMEN: endometrium, office biopsy.
CLINICAL: infertility; biopsy timed to the luteal phase.
GROSS: received in formalin, multiple fragments of tan-red soft tissue, aggregate 1.5 cm, entirely submitted.
MICROSCOPIC: secretory endometrium with glandular and stromal features corresponding to the expected cycle day. No hyperplasia. No inflammation.
reports.conclusion: Secretory endometrium, in phase; consistent with normal luteal function.

documents.title: Infertility Follow-up
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY GROUP
Office visit 06/15/2026

Returns to go over her infertility evaluation. Now 18 months of trying. Periods every 28 days for about 5 days. Lower abdominal pain with menses keeps getting worse, and deep dyspareunia continues. Naproxen helps somewhat.

Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: mild tenderness on deep palpation of the posterior fornix. No adnexal mass palpable. No cervical motion tenderness.

Results:
- Ovulation: confirmed on serial home urinary LH testing.
- Chlamydia and gonorrhea NAAT: negative.
- Hysterosalpingogram: normal uterine cavity, both tubes patent.
- Luteal endometrial biopsy: in phase, consistent with normal luteal function.
- Partner semen analysis: normal.

Assessment: 18 months of infertility with a normal basic evaluation; endometriosis is the likely contributor.

Plan: we discussed next steps, which range from assisted reproduction to surgery. I have referred her to reproductive endocrinology to review treatment options; their office will call to schedule. Continue naproxen as needed.

Thank you for allowing us to share in her care.
